summary: Not captured: the robots rules allow the sign-in address, but no terms document could be found or read, so the check before a capture did not come back clean. No other public source shows the sign-in form. The sign-in page was not loaded.
lookedFor: robots.txt of registro.br, read on the review date: HTTP 200, and none of its rules covers /login/, the catalog sign-in address. It does disallow /2/, /cgi-bin/ and /painel/ among others.

The site's terms: the home page's static HTML is an empty script-application shell without legal links, a static read of /dominio/contrato/ returned no text, and a web search found no terms document on the site. Whether the terms restrict automated access is therefore not established.

A code search on GitHub for the sign-in address: this repository's own catalog, one lookup-tool definition that names the address without any markup, and two documentation files of unrelated projects that were not opened. Nothing found reproduces the form.
neededFromUser: The sign-in page saved from the user's own browser as "Webpage, Complete" and read with the capture tool's --from-file mode, plus the page that follows the first step if the sign-in has two. The site is script-rendered, so the saved file must hold the rendered page, not the empty shell. That would make this class A. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
